requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.1.2-16]	If the Will Flag is set to 1 and If Will Retain is set to 0, the Server MUST publish the Will Message as a non-retained message.
requirements.condition: When Will Flag is 1 and Will Retain is 0
requirements.required_behavior: Publish the Will Message as non-retained.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not publish it as retained.
requirements.why_checkable: The emitted Will publication's retained status can be observed.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.1.2-17]	If the Will Flag is set to 1 and If Will Retain is set to 1, the Server MUST publish the Will Message as a retained message.
requirements.condition: When Will Flag is 1 and Will Retain is 1
requirements.required_behavior: Publish the Will Message as retained.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not publish it as non-retained.
requirements.why_checkable: A later subscription can verify retained storage of the emitted Will.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.1.2-18]	If the User Name Flag is set to 0, a user name MUST NOT be present in the payload.
requirements.condition: When User Name Flag is 0
requirements.forbidden_behavior: A user name MUST NOT be present in the CONNECT payload.
requirements.why_checkable: The flag and payload field sequence can be checked together.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.1.2-19]	If the User Name Flag is set to 1, a user name MUST be present in the payload.
requirements.condition: When User Name Flag is 1
requirements.required_behavior: Include a user name in the CONNECT payload.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: A missing user-name field is forbidden.
requirements.why_checkable: The flag and payload field sequence can be checked together.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.1.2-20]	If the Password Flag is set to 0, a password MUST NOT be present in the payload.
requirements.condition: When Password Flag is 0
requirements.forbidden_behavior: A password MUST NOT be present in the CONNECT payload.
requirements.why_checkable: The flag and payload field sequence can be checked together.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.1.2-21]	If the Password Flag is set to 1, a password MUST be present in the payload.
requirements.condition: When Password Flag is 1
requirements.required_behavior: Include a password in the CONNECT payload.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: A missing password field is forbidden.
requirements.why_checkable: The flag and payload field sequence can be checked together.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.1.2-22]	If the User Name Flag is set to 0, the Password Flag MUST be set to 0.
requirements.condition: When User Name Flag is 0
requirements.required_behavior: Set Password Flag to 0.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The combination User Name Flag=0 and Password Flag=1 is forbidden.
requirements.why_checkable: The two flag bits can be checked for the prohibited combination.

requirements.quote:
[MQTT-3.1.2-23]	It is the responsibility of the Client to ensure that the interval between Control Packets being sent does not exceed the Keep Alive value.
In the absence of sending any other Control Packets, the Client MUST send a PINGREQ Packet.
requirements.condition: While a nonzero Keep Alive interval is active
requirements.required_behavior: Ensure the interval between Control Packets sent by the Client does not exceed Keep Alive.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not remain silent beyond the configured interval.
requirements.why_checkable: Consecutive outbound Control Packet timestamps can be compared with Keep Alive.

requirements.quote:
[MQTT-3.1.2-23]	It is the responsibility of the Client to ensure that the interval between Control Packets being sent does not exceed the Keep Alive value.
In the absence of sending any other Control Packets, the Client MUST send a PINGREQ Packet.
requirements.condition: While Keep Alive is active and the Client has no other Control Packet to send
requirements.required_behavior: Send PINGREQ before the Keep Alive interval is exceeded.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not let the interval expire without another Control Packet or PINGREQ.
requirements.why_checkable: A timed idle Client trace can verify the presence and deadline of PINGREQ.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.1.2-24]	If the Keep Alive value is non-zero and the Server does not receive a Control Packet from the Client within one and a half times the Keep Alive time period, it MUST disconnect the Network Connection to the Client as if the network had failed.
requirements.condition: When Keep Alive is nonzero and no Client Control Packet arrives within 1.5 times that interval
requirements.error_behavior: Disconnect the Client's Network Connection and handle it as a network failure.
requirements.why_checkable: A silent Client and controlled timer allow the threshold and disconnection to be observed.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.1.3-1]	These fields, if present, MUST appear in the order Client Identifier, Will Topic, Will Message, User Name, Password.
requirements.condition: When CONNECT payload fields are present
requirements.required_behavior: Order them as Client Identifier, Will Topic, Will Message, User Name, Password, omitting only absent conditional fields.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not place any present field out of the listed relative order.
requirements.why_checkable: The parsed payload field sequence can be compared with the ordered list.

requirements.quote:
[MQTT-3.1.3-2]	Each Client connecting to the Server has a unique ClientId.
The ClientId MUST be used by Clients and by Servers to identify state that they hold relating to this MQTT Session between the Client and the Server.
requirements.condition: For Clients connecting to a Server
requirements.required_behavior: Use a unique ClientId for each Client.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not allow two connected Clients to share the same effective ClientId.
requirements.why_checkable: The Server's active connections can be checked for duplicate effective identifiers.

requirements.quote:
[MQTT-3.1.3-2]	Each Client connecting to the Server has a unique ClientId.
The ClientId MUST be used by Clients and by Servers to identify state that they hold relating to this MQTT Session between the Client and the Server.
requirements.condition: When a Client identifies state held for an MQTT Session
requirements.required_behavior: Use ClientId as the state identifier.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not identify the Session state independently of ClientId.
requirements.why_checkable: Client persistence and reconnect state can be correlated with ClientId.

requirements.quote:
[MQTT-3.1.3-2]	Each Client connecting to the Server has a unique ClientId.
The ClientId MUST be used by Clients and by Servers to identify state that they hold relating to this MQTT Session between the Client and the Server.
requirements.condition: When a Server identifies state held for an MQTT Session
requirements.required_behavior: Use ClientId as the state identifier.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not identify the Session state independently of ClientId.
requirements.why_checkable: Server state lookup can be tested with distinct and repeated ClientIds.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.1.3-3]	The Client Identifier (ClientId) MUST be present and MUST be the first field in the CONNECT packet payload.
requirements.condition: For every CONNECT payload
requirements.required_behavior: Include ClientId.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: A missing ClientId is forbidden.
requirements.why_checkable: The payload can be parsed and checked for field presence.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.1.3-3]	The Client Identifier (ClientId) MUST be present and MUST be the first field in the CONNECT packet payload.
requirements.condition: For every CONNECT payload
requirements.required_behavior: Place ClientId as the first field.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not place another field before it.
requirements.why_checkable: The first parsed payload field can be inspected.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.1.3-4]	The ClientId MUST be a UTF-8 encoded string as defined in Section 1.5.3.
requirements.condition: When encoding or decoding ClientId
requirements.required_behavior: Use an MQTT UTF-8 encoded string.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use arbitrary binary data or another string representation.
requirements.why_checkable: The length-prefixed bytes can be validated against the MQTT UTF-8 rules.

requirements.quote:
[MQTT-3.1.3-5]	The Server MUST allow ClientIds which are between 1 and 23 UTF-8 encoded bytes in length, and that contain only the characters
"0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ".
requirements.condition: When a ClientId uses only the listed alphanumeric characters
requirements.required_behavior: Accept encoded lengths from 1 through 23 bytes inclusive.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not reject such a ClientId solely because its length is within that range.
requirements.why_checkable: Boundary and interior lengths can be submitted and Server acceptance observed.

requirements.quote:
[MQTT-3.1.3-5]	The Server MUST allow ClientIds which are between 1 and 23 UTF-8 encoded bytes in length, and that contain only the characters
"0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ".
requirements.condition: When a ClientId is 1 through 23 UTF-8 encoded bytes long
requirements.required_behavior: Accept every ClientId composed only of 0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not reject any character from the mandatory alphabet.
requirements.why_checkable: ClientIds covering every listed character can be submitted within the mandatory length range.

requirements.quote:
[MQTT-3.1.3-6]	A Server MAY allow a Client to supply a ClientId that has a length of zero bytes.
However if it does so the Server MUST treat this as a special case and assign a unique ClientId to that Client.
It MUST then process the CONNECT packet as if the Client had provided that unique ClientId.
requirements.condition: When a Client supplies a zero-byte ClientId
requirements.required_behavior: The Server is permitted to accept it.
requirements.why_checkable: MAY supplies no mandatory acceptance or rejection choice.

requirements.quote:
[MQTT-3.1.3-6]	A Server MAY allow a Client to supply a ClientId that has a length of zero bytes.
However if it does so the Server MUST treat this as a special case and assign a unique ClientId to that Client.
It MUST then process the CONNECT packet as if the Client had provided that unique ClientId.
requirements.condition: When the Server accepts a zero-byte ClientId
requirements.required_behavior: Assign a unique ClientId to that Client.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not retain the zero-byte identifier or assign an identifier already in use.
requirements.why_checkable: Multiple zero-ID connections can be checked for distinct effective identifiers.

requirements.quote:
[MQTT-3.1.3-6]	A Server MAY allow a Client to supply a ClientId that has a length of zero bytes.
However if it does so the Server MUST treat this as a special case and assign a unique ClientId to that Client.
It MUST then process the CONNECT packet as if the Client had provided that unique ClientId.
requirements.condition: After assigning a unique ClientId for a zero-byte value
requirements.required_behavior: Process CONNECT as though the Client supplied the assigned identifier.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use the original zero-byte value for subsequent connection processing.
requirements.why_checkable: Session creation and identity-dependent behavior can be compared with an explicit-ID connection.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.1.3-7]	If the Client supplies a zero-byte ClientId, the Client MUST also set CleanSession to 1.
requirements.condition: When the Client supplies a zero-byte ClientId
requirements.required_behavior: Set CleanSession to 1.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The combination zero-byte ClientId and CleanSession=0 is forbidden.
requirements.why_checkable: The payload length and flag bit can be checked in one CONNECT.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.1.3-8]	If the Client supplies a zero-byte ClientId with CleanSession set to 0, the Server MUST respond to the CONNECT Packet with a CONNACK return code 0x02 (Identifier rejected) and then close the Network Connection.
requirements.condition: When zero-byte ClientId is supplied with CleanSession=0
requirements.required_behavior: Send CONNACK with return code 0x02.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not send success or another rejection code.
requirements.why_checkable: The exact CONNACK return code can be observed.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.1.3-8]	If the Client supplies a zero-byte ClientId with CleanSession set to 0, the Server MUST respond to the CONNECT Packet with a CONNACK return code 0x02 (Identifier rejected) and then close the Network Connection.
requirements.condition: After sending the 0x02 CONNACK for zero-byte ClientId with CleanSession=0
requirements.error_behavior: Close the Network Connection after CONNACK.
requirements.why_checkable: The response and connection closure order can be observed.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.1.3-9]	If the Server rejects the ClientId it MUST respond to the CONNECT Packet with a CONNACK return code 0x02 (Identifier rejected) and then close the Network Connection.
requirements.condition: When the Server rejects ClientId
requirements.required_behavior: Send CONNACK with return code 0x02.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not send success or another rejection code.
requirements.why_checkable: The exact CONNACK return code can be observed.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.1.3-9]	If the Server rejects the ClientId it MUST respond to the CONNECT Packet with a CONNACK return code 0x02 (Identifier rejected) and then close the Network Connection.
requirements.condition: After sending 0x02 CONNACK for a rejected ClientId
requirements.error_behavior: Close the Network Connection after CONNACK.
requirements.why_checkable: The response and connection closure order can be observed.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.1.3-10]	The Will Topic MUST be a UTF-8 encoded string as defined in Section ‎1.5.3.
requirements.condition: When encoding or decoding Will Topic
requirements.required_behavior: Use an MQTT UTF-8 encoded string.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use arbitrary binary data or another string representation.
requirements.why_checkable: Will Topic bytes can be validated against the referenced UTF-8 rules.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.1.3-11]	The User Name MUST be a UTF-8 encoded string as defined in Section 1.5.3.
requirements.condition: When encoding or decoding User Name
requirements.required_behavior: Use an MQTT UTF-8 encoded string.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use arbitrary binary data or another string representation.
requirements.why_checkable: User Name bytes can be validated against the referenced UTF-8 rules.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.1.4-1]	The Server MUST validate that the CONNECT Packet conforms to section 3.1 and close the Network Connection without sending a CONNACK if it does not conform.
requirements.condition: When the Server receives CONNECT
requirements.required_behavior: Validate it against section 3.1.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not accept a CONNECT that fails section 3.1.
requirements.why_checkable: The validation predicate aggregates all of section 3.1, whose atomic rules are not present in this chunk, so this item does not define a standalone test input set.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.1.4-1]	The Server MUST validate that the CONNECT Packet conforms to section 3.1 and close the Network Connection without sending a CONNACK if it does not conform.
requirements.condition: When CONNECT does not conform to section 3.1
requirements.why_checkable: Connection termination can be observed after malformed CONNECT.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.1.4-1]	The Server MUST validate that the CONNECT Packet conforms to section 3.1 and close the Network Connection without sending a CONNACK if it does not conform.
requirements.condition: When CONNECT does not conform to section 3.1
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not send CONNACK.
requirements.why_checkable: The outbound packet trace can verify CONNACK absence before closure.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.1.4-2]	If the ClientId represents a Client already connected to the Server then the Server MUST disconnect the existing Client.
requirements.condition: When ClientId represents an already connected Client
requirements.why_checkable: A second connection with the same ClientId can be made and the older connection observed.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.1.4-3]	If CONNECT validation is successful the Server MUST perform the processing of CleanSession that is described in section 3.1.2.4.
requirements.condition: When CONNECT validation succeeds
requirements.required_behavior: Perform CleanSession processing described in section 3.1.2.4.
requirements.why_checkable: The behavior is delegated to another section and is not atomically specified in this chunk.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.1.4-4] 	If CONNECT validation is successful the Server MUST acknowledge the CONNECT Packet with a CONNACK Packet containing a zero return code.
requirements.condition: When CONNECT validation succeeds
requirements.required_behavior: Acknowledge CONNECT with CONNACK.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not omit or substitute the response packet type.
requirements.why_checkable: The response packet type can be observed.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.1.4-4] 	If CONNECT validation is successful the Server MUST acknowledge the CONNECT Packet with a CONNACK Packet containing a zero return code.
requirements.condition: When CONNECT validation succeeds
requirements.required_behavior: Set CONNACK return code to 0.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not send a nonzero rejection code.
requirements.why_checkable: The return-code byte can be inspected.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.1.4-5]	If the Server rejects the CONNECT, it MUST NOT process any data sent by the Client after the CONNECT Packet.
requirements.condition: After the Server rejects CONNECT
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not process any later data from that Client on the rejected connection.
requirements.why_checkable: Post-rejection bytes can be sent and application/protocol side effects monitored.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.2.0-1]	The first packet sent from the Server to the Client MUST be a CONNACK Packet.
requirements.condition: For a newly established Server-to-Client MQTT connection
requirements.required_behavior: Make CONNACK the first Server-sent packet.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not send another Control Packet before CONNACK.
requirements.why_checkable: The Server's initial outbound packet sequence is directly observable.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.2.2-1]	If the Server accepts a connection with CleanSession set to 1, the Server MUST set Session Present to 0 in the CONNACK packet in addition to setting a zero return code in the CONNACK packet.
requirements.condition: When the Server accepts CONNECT with CleanSession=1
requirements.required_behavior: Set Session Present to 0 in CONNACK.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not report an existing Session.
requirements.why_checkable: The input flag and CONNACK Session Present bit can be compared.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.2.2-1]	If the Server accepts a connection with CleanSession set to 1, the Server MUST set Session Present to 0 in the CONNACK packet in addition to setting a zero return code in the CONNACK packet.
requirements.condition: When the Server accepts CONNECT with CleanSession=1
requirements.required_behavior: Set CONNACK return code to 0.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not send a nonzero rejection code.
requirements.why_checkable: The CONNACK return-code byte can be inspected.

requirements.quote:
[MQTT-3.2.2-2]  	If the Server accepts a connection with CleanSession set to 0, the value set in Session Present depends on whether the Server already has stored Session state for the supplied client ID.
If the Server has stored Session state, it MUST set Session Present to 1 in the CONNACK packet.
requirements.condition: When the Server accepts CONNECT with CleanSession=0 and already has stored Session state for ClientId
requirements.required_behavior: Set Session Present to 1 in CONNACK.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not report Session Present=0.
requirements.why_checkable: Preloaded session state, CONNECT flags, and the response bit can be checked together.

requirements.quote:
[MQTT-3.2.2-3]	If the Server does not have stored Session state, it MUST set Session Present to 0 in the CONNACK packet.
This is in addition to setting a zero return code in the CONNACK packet.
requirements.condition: When the Server accepts a connection and has no stored Session state for ClientId
requirements.required_behavior: Set Session Present to 0 in CONNACK.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not report a stored Session.
requirements.why_checkable: Absence of preexisting state and the response bit can be compared.

requirements.quote:
[MQTT-3.2.2-3]	If the Server does not have stored Session state, it MUST set Session Present to 0 in the CONNACK packet.
This is in addition to setting a zero return code in the CONNACK packet.
requirements.condition: When the Server accepts a connection and has no stored Session state for ClientId
requirements.required_behavior: Set CONNACK return code to 0.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not reject the connection under this success condition.
requirements.why_checkable: The CONNACK return code can be inspected.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.2.2-4]	If a server sends a CONNACK packet containing a non-zero return code it MUST set Session Present to 0.
requirements.condition: When CONNACK return code is nonzero
requirements.required_behavior: Set Session Present to 0.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not report an existing Session on a rejected connection.
requirements.why_checkable: The two CONNACK fields can be checked together.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.2.2-5]	If a server sends a CONNACK packet containing a non-zero return code it MUST then close the Network Connection.
requirements.condition: After the Server sends CONNACK with a nonzero return code
requirements.error_behavior: Close the Network Connection after CONNACK.
requirements.why_checkable: Response transmission and subsequent closure can be ordered in a trace.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.2.2-6]	If none of the return codes listed in Table 3.1 – Connect Return code values are deemed applicable, then the Server MUST close the Network Connection without sending a CONNACK.
requirements.condition: When no listed CONNACK return code applies
requirements.why_checkable: A failure outside the listed code cases can be induced and closure observed.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.2.2-6]	If none of the return codes listed in Table 3.1 – Connect Return code values are deemed applicable, then the Server MUST close the Network Connection without sending a CONNACK.
requirements.condition: When no listed CONNACK return code applies
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not send CONNACK.
requirements.why_checkable: The outbound trace can verify response absence before closure.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.3.1-1]	The DUP flag MUST be set to 1 by the Client or Server when it attempts to re-deliver a PUBLISH Packet.
requirements.condition: When a Client attempts to redeliver PUBLISH
requirements.required_behavior: Set DUP to 1.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not mark the redelivery as an initial transmission.
requirements.why_checkable: The Client's retransmitted PUBLISH fixed header can be inspected.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.3.1-1]	The DUP flag MUST be set to 1 by the Client or Server when it attempts to re-deliver a PUBLISH Packet.
requirements.condition: When a Server attempts to redeliver PUBLISH
requirements.required_behavior: Set DUP to 1.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not mark the redelivery as an initial transmission.
requirements.why_checkable: The Server's retransmitted PUBLISH fixed header can be inspected.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.3.1-2]	The DUP flag MUST be set to 0 for all QoS 0 messages.
requirements.condition: For every QoS 0 PUBLISH
requirements.required_behavior: Set DUP to 0.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not set DUP to 1.
requirements.why_checkable: The QoS bits and DUP bit can be checked together.

requirements.quote:
[MQTT-3.3.1-3]	The value of the DUP flag from an incoming PUBLISH packet is not propagated when the PUBLISH Packet is sent to subscribers by the Server.
The DUP flag in the outgoing PUBLISH packet is set independently to the incoming PUBLISH packet, its value MUST be determined solely by whether the outgoing PUBLISH packet is a retransmission.
requirements.condition: When the Server sends a PUBLISH to subscribers after receiving an incoming PUBLISH
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not copy or propagate the incoming DUP value into the outgoing PUBLISH.
requirements.why_checkable: Incoming DUP can be varied while holding outgoing retransmission status constant, and the outgoing bit compared.

requirements.quote:
[MQTT-3.3.1-3]	The value of the DUP flag from an incoming PUBLISH packet is not propagated when the PUBLISH Packet is sent to subscribers by the Server.
The DUP flag in the outgoing PUBLISH packet is set independently to the incoming PUBLISH packet, its value MUST be determined solely by whether the outgoing PUBLISH packet is a retransmission.
requirements.condition: When the Server sets DUP on an outgoing subscriber PUBLISH
requirements.required_behavior: Determine the value solely from whether that outgoing PUBLISH is a retransmission.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not let the incoming PUBLISH DUP value influence it.
requirements.why_checkable: Outgoing initial and retransmission paths can be tested against both possible incoming DUP values.

requirements.quote:
[MQTT-3.3.1-4]	A PUBLISH Packet MUST NOT have both QoS bits set to 1.
If a Server or Client receives a PUBLISH Packet which has both QoS bits set to 1 it MUST close the Network Connection.
requirements.condition: For every PUBLISH packet
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not set both QoS bits to 1.
requirements.why_checkable: The two QoS bits can be checked for the forbidden binary value 11.

requirements.quote:
[MQTT-3.3.1-4]	A PUBLISH Packet MUST NOT have both QoS bits set to 1.
If a Server or Client receives a PUBLISH Packet which has both QoS bits set to 1 it MUST close the Network Connection.
requirements.condition: When a Server or Client receives PUBLISH with QoS bits 11
requirements.why_checkable: The forbidden bit pattern can be injected and connection termination observed.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.3.1-5]	If the RETAIN flag is set to 1, in a PUBLISH Packet sent by a Client to a Server, the Server MUST store the Application Message and its QoS, so that it can be delivered to future subscribers whose subscriptions match its topic name.
requirements.condition: When the Server receives Client PUBLISH with RETAIN=1
requirements.required_behavior: Store the Application Message.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not discard the retained Application Message.
requirements.why_checkable: A later matching subscription can verify persistence of the message.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.3.1-5]	If the RETAIN flag is set to 1, in a PUBLISH Packet sent by a Client to a Server, the Server MUST store the Application Message and its QoS, so that it can be delivered to future subscribers whose subscriptions match its topic name.
requirements.condition: When the Server receives Client PUBLISH with RETAIN=1
requirements.required_behavior: Store the message's QoS with it.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not lose the retained QoS metadata.
requirements.why_checkable: The QoS of later retained delivery can be compared with the stored publication.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.3.1-5]	If the RETAIN flag is set to 1, in a PUBLISH Packet sent by a Client to a Server, the Server MUST store the Application Message and its QoS, so that it can be delivered to future subscribers whose subscriptions match its topic name.
requirements.condition: When a future subscription matches the retained message's Topic Name
requirements.required_behavior: Make the stored Application Message available for delivery to that subscriber.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not make the retained record unusable for future matching delivery.
requirements.why_checkable: Publishing retained data before subscribing provides a direct persistence-and-delivery test.
